If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 5 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment shifts from neutral to positive, adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.8% per day of sentiment change.

In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains flat or negative, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day to reflect diminishing momentum.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in last 3 days, apply a 1.0–1.5% downward correction to forecast in late horizon to avoid overreaction.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows strong upward trend, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias in mid-horizon to prevent overfitting to recent momentum.
